`session_id.clone()` is unnecessary here: the function takes `session_id: Option<String>` by value, the prior trace block only borrowed via `.as_deref()` (lines 970/972), and `session_id` is unused after this point in `bot_chat`. Pass by value to avoid the allocation + cloner round-trip on the hot chat-completion path.

```rust
crate::memory::extract::maybe_extract_from_session(
    extract_app,
    session_id,                 // pass by value, no clone
    stop.is_interactive(),
);
```

Hook fires unconditionally even when the conversation was aborted by `/stop` (`aborted = stop.stopped()`). Trace module treats Aborted as a distinct outcome that suppresses recording in several rules, but extract has no symmetric gating. A user who issues `/stop` mid-conversation will still get their partial chat mined for facts ~30min later. If that's not intended, gate the call with `if !aborted { ... }` or pass `aborted` into `maybe_extract_from_session` so it can early-return alongside the existing gates. Worth confirming against the U16 spec — currently the asymmetry is silent.

`apply_ops` breaks the U17 "旧签名委托默认值" contract. The spec mandates a `_with` variant where the old signature still compiles and delegates to defaults; `store::insert_item` and `panel::import_items` follow this pattern (old fn calls `*_with(..., &StoreParams::default())`), but `apply_ops` was directly modified to take `sp: &store::StoreParams` with no default-delegating wrapper. As a direct consequence, every call site — including all 8 tests in this file plus the production `run_consolidation` site — had to be edited to thread `&StoreParams::default()` through. Consider adding an `apply_ops_with` that takes the params and an `apply_ops(conn, ops, embs, now_ms)` wrapper that delegates to `apply_ops_with(..., &StoreParams::default())`, then keep these test bodies on the bare signature.

comments.content: Confirmed finding #1 still applies: `session_id` is `Option<String>` and is unused after this point (the only prior usage on lines 970/972 borrows via `as_deref()`). Pass by value with `session_id` directly to avoid the clone allocation on the hot path — every chat turn pays this cost, even though `maybe_extract_from_session` already filters out `None`/empty values internally.

Confirmed finding #2 still applies: the U16 extract hook fires unconditionally on every interactive turn, including when the conversation was aborted via `/stop` (`aborted = stop.stopped()` is already computed on line 967). Trace distinguishes `Aborted` from `Success` and suppresses sampling for Aborted in several rules, but extract has no symmetric gating. A `/stop` mid-conversation still triggers an LLM extraction call against the partial transcript — wasted tokens and a non-insert memory candidate that the user explicitly walked away from. Either short-circuit here with `if aborted { return; }` before the call, or push the `aborted` flag through to `maybe_extract_from_session` so the gate sits next to the existing throttle / mode / control gates (which is more in line with the spec's 「失败静默」contract: a user-aborted turn is logically a failed turn for extraction purposes).

API inconsistency: `hybrid_search_with` takes `top_n: usize` and `decay_days: f64` as separate positional arguments, while its sibling `injection_snapshot_with`� (lines 175-182) accepts the whole `&RankParams` struct. The same module now has two divergent parameterization patterns for the same kind of tuning. Consider taking `&RankParams`� here as well so callers can do `RankParams::of(&tuning)` uniformly and `top_n`/`decay_days` stay encapsulated; the body would simply use `p.top_n` and `p.decay_days`. As-is, callers have to manually destructure tuning and pass two scalar args to `hybrid_search_with`, which defeats the� point of having� `RankParams` in the first place.

Dead/incomplete parameterization: `hybrid_search_with` is `pub` but has no external caller. The only consumer of `hybrid_search` (e.g. `tool_recall_facts` in memory/mod.rs:586, `panel.rs:104`, tests) still goes through the legacy wrapper which hard-codes `30.0` for `decay_days`.�� That means the new `memoryTuning.decayDays` setting is silently ignored on the recall path even though the U17 design calls for it to thread through `recall_facts`. Either update every external caller to use `hybrid_search_with` (� ideally with the `&RankParams` signature proposed above) or mark this `pub(crate)` until���it is wired up.

Magic number `30.0`: the three `usize` defaults reuse the existing `MEMORY_TOP_N` / `MEMORY_RECENT_N` / `MEMORY_LESSON_N` constants but `decay_days` is hard-coded inline. If anyone grep-references "the 30-day decay" after this change (e.g. docs, store.rs, panel.rs) there is nothing for them to find. Add a sibling constant such as `pub const MEMORY_DECAY_DAYS: f64 = 30.0;` and reference it from both `Default::default()` and the legacy `hybrid_score` / `hybrid_search` wrappers so the default lives in exactly one place.

`RankParams` is a public type whose fields are referenced across `injection_snapshot_with`, `hybrid_search_with`, and (once� wired up) `hybrid_score_with`. None� of the four fields carry a doc comment explaining the units / semantics. At a minimum `decay_days` (the time constant of `exp(-age/decay)`), `top_n`/`recent_n`/`lesson_n` (per-section item counts; truncation is `take(n)`, so 0 yields empty sections) deserve a one-liner each. Without it future callers have to read memory/mod.rs's `MemoryTuning::clamped` and� the score formula�� to reverse-engineer meaning.

comments.content: `hybrid_score_with` does not validate `decay_days`. The expression `(-age_days / decay_days).exp()` produces `NaN` if `decay_days` is `0.0` / negative / `NaN`, and produces `inf` if the magnitude exceeds `f64` range. `NaN` then silently breaks `scored.sort_by(... b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal))` in both `injection_snapshot_with` and `hybrid_search_with` — `partial_cmp` returns `None` for `NaN`, falling back to `Equal`, so `NaN`-scored items land in non-deterministic positions. `RankParams::default()` and `MemoryTuning::clamped()` happen to enforce a positive value, but `RankParams` is a `pub` struct with `pub decay_days: f64` — any external caller can hand-craft a pathological value. Either guard at the top of `hybrid_score_with` (e.g. `debug_assert!(decay_days.is_finite() && decay_days > 0.0, "decay_days must be finite and positive")`) or normalize via `.max(f64::MIN_POSITIVE)` before use.

comments.content: The capacity test only exercises `embedding: None` (which skips dedup entirely per the comment in `insert_item_with`). The `len() == 1` assertion therefore does not distinguish "eviction succeeded" from "dedup accidentally merged the two items" — only happens to pass because `None` bypasses dedup. Consider also asserting `all[0].content == "第二条"` is checked AND adding a third item with a fresh embedding to confirm capacity continues to evict past dedup. (The content assertion at line 665 already provides this protection in part; no change required, but worth flagging for the next reviewer if `None` semantics ever change.)

The dedup threshold test relies on the implicit arithmetic fact that `cosine(onehot(0), tilted(0.99))` is exactly `0.99` (because `tilted` constructs `v[0]=w, v[1]=sqrt(1-w²)` and both vectors are L2-normalized). This is correct but not documented at the test site — if a future refactor changes `tilted`'s construction, the test silently passes/fails for the wrong reason. Recommend a one-line comment near the helper or test recording the expected cosine so future readers don't have to redo the math.

comments.content:
[medium] Server interface uses `autoExtract?: string | null` while state is `"off" | "auto" | "confirm"`. The validator at lines 549–555 then needs a double `as` cast to satisfy `Array.includes`, which bypasses TS narrowing and silently accepts any cast value. Tighten the interface (or extract an `isAutoExtract` guard) so the cast disappears.

Also: the expression `c.memoryControl?.autoExtract as "off" | "auto" | "confirm"` is repeated twice. Hoist it to a `const raw = c.memoryControl?.autoExtract;` and use one boolean guard for clarity.

[low] The mode set `["off", "auto", "confirm"]` and the labels (`关闭 / 自动入库 / 需确认`) are duplicated here (initial state default at line 397, validator at line 551, UI `.map([…])`). Extract a single `const AUTO_EXTRACT_MODES = [{ value: "off", label: "关闭", aria: "自动记忆抽取：关闭" }, …] as const` at module scope and derive the union with `typeof AUTO_EXTRACT_MODES[number]["value"]`; the validator and UI both consume it.

[low] Redundant `as` cast on a `null` literal into a union that already includes `null` — the cast on `lastRunAt` two lines above is equally redundant. TypeScript will accept `memoryTuning: null,` and `lastRunAt: null,` here without the explicit annotation, since the useState generic already declares the union type.

In `mem_pending_approve`, `pending_delete(&conn, &[*id])?` runs unconditionally after the `match`, including when `insert_item_with` returned `Err` (the `_ => report.skipped += 1` arm catches `Err(_)` alongside the `Ok((RejectedFull/ReusedForeignMerge, _))` outcomes). A transient DB error during insert therefore silently drops the pending row the user just approved — the UI reports "skipped" but the entry is gone, so the user can't retry. `pending_delete` should only run when the insert actually wrote (Inserted or Merged); on insert error, leave the pending row in place so the user can retry.

Note: `InsertOutcome` (see `memory/store.rs`) has variants `Inserted`, `Merged`, `RejectedFull`, `RefusedForeignMerge` — all returned as `Ok(...)`. Only `Result::Err(_)` is the actual transient failure that should preserve pending.

The `AutoExtract::Off => {}` arm in `run_extract` is unreachable: `maybe_extract_from_session` early-returns at line 280 when `mode == AutoExtract::Off` and never spawns the task with `Off`. Keeping a no-op arm risks silently masking a future refactor that removes the early-return gate (e.g., if someone deletes the early-return, `Off` would silently swallow the entire extract pipeline without producing any feedback). Either remove the arm (and rely on the caller-side check) or make it `unreachable!()` with a comment so a regression is loud.

`LAST_EXTRACT_MS` is a purely process-local `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, i64>>>`. An app restart resets every session's throttle window, so the first session-end after launch will always trigger extraction regardless of how recently it ran in the previous process. For users who restart frequently this effectively doubles LLM spend for the auto-extract path. The module doc claims the 30-minute throttle is the "LLM cost first gate" — the gate is bypassed on every restart. Consider either persisting last-extract-ms to the DB (cheap write at extraction completion) or noting this explicitly in the doc comment so reviewers/users aren't surprised by the gap.

comments.content: `pending_insert` accepts any `kind`/`content`/empty strings without validating against the same contract `parse_extract` enforces (whitelist + non-empty). Currently the only caller (`run_extract`) feeds `parse_extract`-filtered data, but the function is private only by convention (no compile-time `any` enforcement) and the contract drifts the moment a future caller is added. Recommend an explicit check here: `if !EXTRACT_KINDS.contains(&kind) || content.trim().is_empty() { return Err(...); }`. Mirrors the table contract and matches the existing `importance.clamp(1,5)` discipline a few lines below.

`mem_pending_approve` doesn't deduplicate `ids` before phase 1. If the frontend ever passes a duplicate (e.g., a multi-select UI bug or a stale row that was re-sent), `pending_get` returns `Some` for each occurrence and the same row is pushed into `rows` twice. Phase 2 then computes an embedding twice (wasted ONNX inference), phase 3 runs `insert_item_with` twice (the second becomes `Merged` via the existing dedup), and the report ends up over-counting (`merged += 2` for what is actually 1 merge). Add a `let mut seen = HashSet::new(); ids.iter().filter(|id| seen.insert(**id))` step up front, or `ids.sort_unstable(); ids.dedup()` before the loop.

`pending_delete(&conn, &[*id])?` propagates Err mid-loop, so a transient DB error on iteration k leaves iterations k+1..N unprocessed (their pending rows still present, no `insert_item_with` ever called) and the assembled `report` is lost (the function returns Err instead). Earlier iterations k' < k have already done `insert_item_with` + `pending_delete` and are committed. The caller-side self-heal is real (re-running approve re-fetches the remaining pending rows), but the partial commit is a code smell: prefer either wrapping the loop in a `conn.transaction()` so insert+delete are atomic per row, or collecting (success_count, errors) and returning Err only after the loop completes. Right now this is a different shape of the same partial-commit pathology already flagged just above the loop.
